step_by_step_reasoning: The whiteboard shows a microservice decomposition architecture for Pushpay. The architecture features two client/monolith services represented by EC2 compute icons: a Giving monolith (.NET) and an Apps platform (Node). Both send GraphQL/API sign-in and sign-up requests to an Identity Service running on Amazon ECS. ECS persists event-sourced data into Amazon DynamoDB and publishes full event streams to Amazon Kinesis (KinesisDataStream). Kinesis then routes sync events back to the Giving monolith (.NET) to complete the feedback loop. Additionally, an AWS X-Ray icon is present for tracing/monitoring across services, and a hand-drawn SQL Server database (RDS) is located under the Giving monolith.

graph.notes: The architecture illustrates breaking down a .NET/SQL Server monolith into microservices running on ECS, using DynamoDB for event sourcing, Kinesis for distributing events back to the monolith, and X-Ray for tracing.
